claims.claim: Upgrade/install --repair built on the production invalidation primitive (platform Cache.invalidate) clears exactly the manifest-owned derived paths (state/cache entries, state/derived-index) and leaves every user-data path byte-identical (pre/post tree hash equal over state/notes, state/profiles, state/user-settings.json, commands.json).

Both-states control: a planted user file survives byte-identical and a planted derived-cache file is removed by the same upgrade; under the deferred (no-op) upgrade mutant the derived state survives, so the assertions fire on the broken state.

Regression seed (_USER-PROMPTS.md:11347): a known-broken rollback that wipes state/ removes user data (detector fires), while the correct rollback preserves user data and installed commands byte-identically and still clears derived cache.

negative_controls.description: No-op upgrade leaves planted derived-cache files in place, so the probe's owned-paths-emptiness assertions fail there - the detector is silent on the good state and fires on the deferred state.
Known-broken rollback (rmtree of state/) deletes user notes/profiles; the tree-hash equality assertion fails there and only there.

implementation.production_primitive: platform/plugin/cache.py Cache.invalidate (EOL-stable hashing; never touches quarantine)
